# Canadian Patents Database - Help - General information

## Background

The Canadian Patents Database (referred to as "the database" throughout this guide) is an interactive search tool designed to help you create simple and powerful searches on Canadian patent information.

The database contains applications and patents from 1869 to the present and is updated on a daily basis.

The electronically available patent information includes patent documents and bibliographic and text data.

Searches are performed using only the bibliographic and text data fields, and return a list of matching applications/patents. While documents are not searchable, they can be viewed for any specific application or patent listed in the search results.

The availability of searchable data varies by field and time period, as outlined below:

  * Bibliographic data (e.g., titles, names, classifications) – available from 1869
  * Text data (e.g., abstract, claims) – available for patents issued after August 15, 1978
  * Issue date – available from 1869
  * Filing date – available for patents issued after August 15, 1978
  * Priority and national entry dates – available for patents issued after October 1, 1989
  * Documents – available from January 1, 1869 (cover pages and abstracts from 1975)

## Currency of information

The information for applications filed directly with the Patent Office will typically be available in the database by the end of the day on which they become open to public inspection. Because all parts of an application are not required at the time of the filing, some data may be absent.

The information for Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) applications that enter the Patent Office are delayed from being available in the database because of normal processing restraints.

The information for New Act patents (patent numbers greater than 2,000,000) will normally be updated on the day of the issuance of the patent.

While every effort is made to ensure the accuracy and currency of the data in the database, occasional issues may arise. Please see the "Disclaimer" section. Those filed on or after October 1, 1989, are classified according to the International Patent Classification (IPC) system. The present version of the IPC can be consulted on the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)'s International Patent Classification (IPC) page.

## Database overview

The database allows you to search for applications opened to public inspection and for granted patents by number, by text, as well as through various fields and criteria. You can also limit your searches to specific date ranges based on any date field. For detailed guidance on conducting searches, please refer to the "Search" and the "Search syntax" sections of this guide.

You can use the:

  1. Number Search to locate a specific application/patent using its number
  2. Basic Search to find applications/patents containing a specific word or phrase
  3. Boolean Search to search applications/patents using words or phrases across various text fields, with boolean connectors (AND or OR) to narrow or expand results

The database includes some information obtained from external sources, such as WIPO. CIPO cannot guarantee the quality, accuracy, reliability or timeliness of information obtained from third parties. Additionally, some of the information may not be subject to the Government of Canada's web standards, the Privacy Act or the Official Languages Act and, therefore, is available only in the language in which it was provided. Users wishing to rely upon this information should consult directly with the source of the information.

This database is intended for informational use only. For legal purposes, users are advised to consult the official documents available from the Patent Office. Business decisions should not be based solely on data retrieved from this database.

## Conditions of use

The database is provided for use by the general public. Due to equipment and bandwidth limitations, it is not intended as a source for bulk downloads of patent data. Information on obtaining bulk data is available on the IP Horizons: Download intellectual property data page.

Please note that users generating unusually high volumes of daily access (1,000 or more) may be restricted from accessing the database without prior notice, as this may impact service availability for others.

## Privacy

Please note that communications between the database and its users are not confidential. Therefore, any information you wish to keep private—such as search queries—should not be submitted through the database.

When using a public or shared computer, we recommend clearing your browser's cache to remove any stored pages.

To learn how to protect your personal and confidential information when submitting documents to CIPO, and how to request corrections or removals from the database, visit the Protect your privacy on the Canadian Patents Database page.

## For further assistance

For questions or assistance related to the database, please contact the CIPO Client Service Centre.

Download records of patent applications and granted patents filed with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office. We offer a full historical collection and provide new and updated records weekly.

Note: We only publish patent applications after a confidentiality period. This period is up to 18 months after the earliest filing date of an application.

## Format

We provide this data in XML. It follows World Intellectual Property Organization standard ST.36.

Note: On May 5, 2022 , CIPO ended the production of 2 of its patent data products: 1) Administrative Status (XML); and 2) Bibliographic and full text (XML). They've been replaced by our Patent XML ST.36 product, which combines the elements of both formats into a single XML file.

# Patent data and images

## Service interruption – Next Generation Patents

As part of the Canadian Intellectual Property Office's Next Generation Patents initiative, we are currently experiencing technical challenges affecting the quality of patent products published on IP Horizons. We will continue to publish files, but there may be some missing data and/or data errors.

Please note that we are actively working to resolve these issues, and affected products will be reissued as needed. We appreciate your understanding and apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. Updates will be provided as they become available.

Download electronic scans of newly granted and laid open patent applications filed with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office. We provide access to new image files weekly.

Note: We only publish patent applications after a confidentiality period. This period is up to 18 months after the earliest filing date of an application.

## Format

We have been providing this data in PDF format since January 2025. Prior to that, this data was available in multi-page Tag Image File Format (TIFF).

All patent image files contain cover pages once they are generated by the office and PDF or TIFF images of the first 250 pages for each section of the patent document.

## Record and data content

Patent image collections are provided for both patent applications and granted patents. Patent data is open to public inspection after a confidentiality period of up to 18 months after the earliest filing date of an application. Each patent image collection includes scanned images (in PDF or TIFF format) of the patent application, along with additional text content of the title and abstract.

Images include:

  * Cover page (IP number, name and address for applicant, inventor and agents, dates of filing and publication, issue and national entry, text searchable title and abstract, cover page image, priorities)
  * Patent description
  * Claims (a legal description of the scope of the patent and defines the specific attributes of the invention that are protected from infringement)
  * Drawings

  * Weekly files
  * Historical files

## How it works

Our cutting edge APIs allow you to transact with IP right databases at any time, fully integrate your systems and even develop your own software.

You can use our APIs to:

  * Submit IP right requests, including new applications and renewals
  * Get data from trade mark, patent and design search platforms
  * Make payments
  * Retrieve correspondence.

You can't:

  * File evidence for trade mark or patent oppositions.

### Who should use APIs?

Our API service is perfect for:

  * High-volume customers who frequently transact with us and access our data, such as attorney firms
  * IP software developers.

### How much does it cost?

There isn't a fee to connect our APIs to your system, however, you'll need to pay the required fee for any actions, such as filing a new application.

## Benefits of API integration

There's plenty of reasons to consider integration of our APIs, including:

  * Access to real time IP right data
  * Improved visibility of lodgement status
  * Integration of your system with ours, allowing IP right searches directly from your own system
  * Automation of correspondence management, searching and polling
  * Ability to develop your own software
  * Reduction in error trade, time to lodge requests and admin effort.

## How to get started

To register for APIs, you'll need to create an account with our API developer portal.

You can use the portal to:

  * Request API access
  * Understand the API specifications
  * Review the API security protocols.

# Patent researcher datasets: Bibliographic, full text and administrative status data (CSV and TXT)

## Service interruption – Q4 patent researcher dataset

Due to ongoing maintenance activities related to the Canadian Intellectual Property Office's Next Generation Patents initiative, the patent researcher dataset will not be refreshed for the final quarter of the 2024–2025 fiscal year. This represents the period from January 1 to March 31, 2025. We appreciate your understanding and apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

Download records of patent applications and granted patents filed with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO). We provide new and updated records on a quarterly basis.

The files on this page consist of tables with data from multiple patent records, as opposed to our XML files, which are individual to each patent record. To download patent data in XML format, please visit our Patent ST.36 page.

Note: We only publish patent applications after a confidentiality period. This period is up to 18 months, starting after the earliest filing date of an application.

## Format

We provide this data in a combination of CSV and TXT formats. Compared to XML, these formats are more accessible to researchers. This aligns with CIPO's goal to encourage research in the field of intellectual property.

## Information included

  * Bibliographic data: applicant names, title of invention, critical application processing dates, etc.
  * Title and abstract text: a short description of the invention
  * Claims: a legal description of the scope and specific attributes of a patent
  * Disclosure and description: a full description of the invention
  * Priority claims: the same or related inventions by the same applicants or owners.
  * International Patent Classification (IPC) codes: a classification system used to classify and search patent documents based on their technical field(s).

Note: We scan the applications using optical character recognition. These files do not represent a legal copy.

## Data structure

This database consists of 7 tables:

  * PT_Main
  * PT_Priority_Claim
  * PT_Interested_Party
  * PT_Abstract
  * PT_Disclosure
  * PT_Claim
  * PT_IPC_Classification

PT_Main is the master table that contains the patent number as the primary key, as well as basic information regarding the patent application. All other tables can be linked to the PT_Main table through the patent number. Due to the amount of data, we have split some tables into multiple smaller tables to make them more manageable for downloading.

# Canadian Patents Database - Help - Documents and downloading capabilities

## Viewing and downloading documents

To view a document, first locate the relevant application or patent. From the "Patent Summary" page, go to the "Documents" tab and click the link in the "Document Description" column for the document you wish to view.

To download one or more documents, select the corresponding checkboxes in the first column and click either the "Download Selected in PDF format (Zip Archive)" or "Download Selected as Single PDF" button.

Documents are available for download in Adobe Acrobat^{TM} PDF format using standard web browser functions. Adobe Acrobat Reader can be downloaded free of charge from the Adobe website.

If you experience any issues accessing content, please contact the CIPO Client Service Centre.

Note: If you have difficulties with downloading multiple files, please try splitting the download into smaller groups of files and try downloading again. If you have any difficulty accessing content, please contact the CIPO Client Service Centre.

## Downloading biological sequence listings

The biological sequence listings (BSL) can be downloaded in electronic text format. All BSLs that CIPO has processed in electronic format are available for each patent application. Some BSLs can be very large and may take a substantial amount of time to download. All BSLs are provided as filed by the applicants. BSL filenames that end with an extension such as.PEP or.SEQ have been modified by CIPO and are for searching purposes only.

If you experience any issues accessing content, please contact the CIPO Client Service Centre.

## Ordering paper copies of documents

To obtain a paper copy of a document, please complete CIPO's Order copies of IP documents form.

## Other types of data

We also have searchable online databases – known as open IP data – where you can access information on IP rights applications.
